Adult female False gharials reach a maximum total length of approximately 400 centimeters [Li = approximately 400 centimeters], while males attain a significantly larger ultimate body size of around 500 centimeters [Li = around 500 centimeters]. This pronounced sexual dimorphism in length is a well-documented characteristic of the species, likely related to intrasexual competition and male-biased territorial behavior. Field surveys and captive records consistently indicate that both sexes reach reproductive maturity, or puberty, at a total length of roughly 275 centimeters [Lp = roughly 275 centimeters], which corresponds to a size range of about 2.5 to 3 meters. Reaching this threshold marks the onset of gonadal activity and the ability to participate in breeding events, though actual nesting may be deferred until individuals acquire adequate body condition and establish a suitable territory.

The eggs of Tomistoma schlegelii, which are deposited in mound nests constructed from vegetation and soil, have an average wet weight of 155 grams [Ww0 = 155 grams] shortly after oviposition. This substantial egg mass provides a rich yolk reserve that supports embryonic development throughout the incubation period. Under controlled laboratory conditions maintained at 29 °C [T = 29 °C], hatching occurs after approximately 95 days [ab = approximately 95 days], a developmental duration consistent with values reported for other large-bodied crocodylians at similar thermal regimes. The newly emerged hatchlings, which are lecithotrophic and depend entirely on their yolk reserves for the first several days, measure around 30 centimeters in total length upon emergence from the eggshell.

The maximum reproductive rate in False gharials is constrained by a combination of environmental temperature and the species' slow life-history pace. Under thermal conditions typical of their native Southeast Asian swamps and riverine habitats (23 °C [T = 23 °C]), females produce between 20 and 60 eggs per clutch [N_R_i = between 20 and 60 eggs per clutch], with a single clutch deposited each year [F_R_i = single clutch deposited each year]. This yields approximately 40 offspring per year [Ri = approximately 40 offspring per year] at 23 °C [T = 23 °C]. The relatively high variation in clutch size is thought to reflect differences in maternal body size and nutritional status.

Adult female False gharials attain an ultimate wet weight of approximately 170,000 grams [Wwi = approximately 170,000 grams], a value derived from scaling relationships based on a 327-centimeter female weighing 93 kilograms. Males, which are the larger sex, reach a substantially greater asymptotic mass of about 210,000 grams [Wwi = about 210,000 grams]. This considerable weight difference is consistent with the species' marked length dimorphism and is likely linked to the energetic demands of male-male combat for access to nesting females. The species shows a relatively slow growth trajectory, with individuals requiring many years to approach these ultimate body sizes.

Under the stable thermal conditions of 23 °C [T = 23 °C], which approximate the mean annual temperatures within the species' natural distribution, both female and male False gharials reach sexual maturity at roughly 20 years [tp = roughly 20 years] of age, and the maximum recorded longevity in the wild is estimated at approximately 80 years [am = approximately 80 years] at 23 °C [T = 23 °C]. The AnAge database reports a maximum lifespan of 24.7 years for this species, though the discrepancy may reflect different populations or data sources.
